newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Tietmeyer says dollar/mark should not rise further.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says dollar/mark should not rise further.

text.p: German Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said in an interview recorded on Monday and due to be broadcast in Hungary next week that he was against any further rise in the dollar against the mark.

"We are not interested that the mark should be devalued (further)," he said. "The recent rise was only a correction process but we are not interested in a correction process that would go beyond tolerable limits."
Tietmeyer told Hungarian Radio the current level of the mark against the dollar was "absolutely correct". ....
The dollar stood at 1.69 on most markets on Monday, when Tietmeyer spoke.
"The development of a currency rate with a stronger dollar is to a large extent a correction of an exaggerated development of the past," he said.

"The correction is good and necessary because the overvaluing of past years made competitiveness of the German economy very difficult but we believe that with the present exchange rates... the conditions have to be created so that the (German) competitiveness should be lasting."
"The labour forces have to adapt...their readiness for mobility and flexibility, adapting themselves to changed conditions.
"Of course we are not interested in an overvalued currency but we are concerned that the mark should be valued correctly and we have the impression that the value of the mark is all right now."

Tietmeyer was speaking in an interview given to Hungarian radio in Franfurt on Monday which is to be broadcast to coincide with the arrival in Hungary next Tuesday of German president Roman Herzog for a three-day visit.
